title: groundwater
intro:
The ’groundwater’ component is responsible for specifying the groundwater table
at each timestep.

sections.name: common
sections.desc: All groundwater models can log height.

attrs.name: height
attrs.doc: Groundwater level. Positive numbers indicate free drainage.

sections.text:
All groundwater models can log height.
  < common      >

Log Variables
    height: number [cm]
     Groundwater level. Positive numbers indicate free drainage.

sections.name: aquitard
sections.desc:
A ‘common’ model (see 45.1, page 225) build into Daisy.
   Aquitard groundwater, free drainage.
sections.sig:
< aquitard (K aquitard 0.001 [cm/h])
                (Z aquitard 200 [cm])
                (h aquifer h aquifer )
                (pressure table pressure table ) >

attrs.name: Z aquitard
attrs.doc:
Thickness of the aquitard. The aquitard begins below the bottommost soil
     horizon.

attrs.name: h aquifer
attrs.doc:
Pressure potential in the aquifer below the aquitard. By default. this is
     Z aquitard. You can alternatively specify the pressure as a virtual groundwa-
     ter level. See ’pressure table’.

attrs.name: pressure table
attrs.doc:
Optional component
     Height of groundwater the corresponds to the pressure in the aquifer.
        If you drilled a well down to the aquifer, this is number what the water level
        in the well would be as height above ground (a negative number). This is
        different from the actual groundwater table, because the aquitart block the
        water, and the pipes lead the water away. You can alternatively specify the
        pressure directly, with ’h aquifer’.

sections.text:
A ‘common’ model (see 45.1, page 225) build into Daisy.
   Aquitard groundwater, free drainage.
  < aquitard (K aquitard 0.001 [cm/h])
                (Z aquitard 200 [cm])
                (h aquifer h aquifer )
                (pressure table pressure table ) >
    K aquitard : number [cm/h]
     Parameter (default 0.001)
     Conductivity of the aquitard.
    Z aquitard : number [cm]
     Parameter (default 200)
     Thickness of the aquitard. The aquitard begins below the bottommost soil
     horizon.
    h aquifer : number [cm]
     Optional state variable
     Pressure potential in the aquifer below the aquitard. By default. this is
     Z aquitard. You can alternatively specify the pressure as a virtual groundwa-
     ter level. See ’pressure table’.
    pressure table: depth component (see chapter 34)
     Optional component
     Height of groundwater the corresponds to the pressure in the aquifer.

        If you drilled a well down to the aquifer, this is number what the water level
        in the well would be as height above ground (a negative number). This is
        different from the actual groundwater table, because the aquitart block the
        water, and the pipes lead the water away. You can alternatively specify the
        pressure directly, with ’h aquifer’.

sections.name: file
sections.desc:
A ‘common’ model (see 45.1, page 225) build into Daisy.
   Read groundwater table from a file.

attrs.name: file
attrs.doc:
Name of file to read data from. The format of each line in the file is ’YEAR
        MONTH DAY HEIGHT’, where HEIGHT should in cm above ground (i.e. a
        negative number). Linear interpolation is used between the datapoints.

attrs.name: offset
attrs.doc: Add this to depth from file.

sections.text:
A ‘common’ model (see 45.1, page 225) build into Daisy.
   Read groundwater table from a file.
  < file file
           (offset 0 [cm]) >

       file: string (see section 4.1.5)
        Parameter
        Name of file to read data from. The format of each line in the file is ’YEAR
        MONTH DAY HEIGHT’, where HEIGHT should in cm above ground (i.e. a
        negative number). Linear interpolation is used between the datapoints.

       offset: number [cm]
        Parameter (default 0)
        Add this to depth from file.

sections.name: static
sections.desc:
